prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (alias/call sign: Juniper) is the region’s primary continuous intake, triage-support, ambulance-dispatch, and coordination point under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols. It maintains a shared operational picture; jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local-policy responsibility. It creates incident records through controlled intake, compares reported conditions with zone coverage, and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead. Call Taker Mara (radio alias: Larkspur) confirms location before medical details: asks street address, municipality, building/floor/entrance, callback number, age, consciousness, breathing, reason for help, symptom onset if reliably estimated, and access barriers. Mara repeats the address and checks nearby landmarks; distinguishes observed symptoms from secondhand reports, updates unresolved locations using focused questions, and stays engaged if new information could change priority or access. Mara produces Caller Location Correction Slip when address clarification must be documented. Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch, checks entered locations against available address/map data, and receives incident requests; operational staff verify displayed information is current. Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and seek guidance beyond delegated authority. Triage Supervisor reviews/confirms priority and coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch as demand/access changes. Regional Medical Director sets clinical triage policies/protocol limits. Shift Commander (alias/call sign: Sundial) manages coordination, continuity, conflicts, surge priorities, escalation, and reviews readiness concerns for repositioning/local coverage, without superseding clinical authority or Paramedic Crew scene judgment. Paramedic Crew assesses/treats within scope and protocols and reports access barriers and vehicle-readiness concerns through established communications. Readiness is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or route/access changes. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) monitors Regional Radio Network, checks channels/backup procedures at shift start, and supports communications; radio checks test weak coverage. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors availability, servicing, defects, and coverage constraints; produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized battery replacement. Readiness checks cover staffing, communications, supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, and maintenance restrictions. Data Quality Officer checks dispatch-record completeness, consistency, and information-handling compliance. Defined response zones reflect distance, roads, and ambulance capacity; boundaries are maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed after road, population, or agreement changes. Each zone has primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center; dispatch considers travel time, restrictions, weather, closures, and crews verify changing conditions before constrained routes. New part:
S066: The Hospital Liaison Desk supports intake coordination by confirming facility capabilities and clarifying hospital contact pathways.
S067: The Hospital Liaison Desk checks whether a reported destination preference is compatible with current facility capabilities.
S068: When a facility constraint affects coordination, the Hospital Liaison Desk records the constraint in the incident notes.
S069: The Hospital Liaison Desk produces the Bedside Arrival Receipt when an ambulance arrival has been confirmed.
S070: The Hospital Liaison Desk provides current facility information through established coordination channels without delaying emergency call intake.
S071: The Triage Supervisor reviews incidents when the reported symptoms or uncertainty warrant clinical escalation.
S072: The Data Quality Officer monitors intake records for recurring gaps in location or medical detail.
S073: Call Taker Mara updates the incident record when a caller provides new information before dispatch decisions are finalized.
S074: The Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S075: Clinical triage begins after Call Taker Mara has captured the caller's reported symptoms, location, and immediate hazards.
S076: The recorded information provides an initial basis for assigning urgency and does not replace clinical reassessment as new information arrives.
S077: Triage Supervisor reviews incidents with uncertain severity, conflicting reports, or signs of rapid deterioration.
S078: Priority is based on the immediacy of threat to life, the likely time sensitivity of care, and the risk of deterioration while awaiting response.
S079: Incidents indicating an immediate threat receive the highest available response priority and prompt dispatch action.
S080: Incidents without an immediate threat are prioritized according to the expected harm from delay and the patient's reported condition.
S081: When essential information is missing, Triage Supervisor directs focused clarification while ensuring that information gathering does not delay an urgent response.
S082: Triage Supervisor escalates clinically ambiguous or unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director for guidance when time permits.
S083: Regional Medical Director provides clinical policy guidance and does not replace the operational authority responsible for dispatch decisions.
S084: Triage Supervisor sends the Pediatric Acuity Note.
S085: Triage Supervisor is known operationally as Copperfield.
S086: Data Quality Officer is known operationally as Pebble.
S087: Data Quality Officer monitors incident records for missing, inconsistent, or duplicated information that could impair triage or dispatch.
S088: Data Quality Officer sends the Duplicate Incident Audit Memo.
